checks.name: positive controls respond
checks.why: a vaccine antigen the model cannot respond to would be useless

checks.name: negative controls do not
checks.detail: every one of the 4 negative controls gives exactly 0
checks.why: self proteins and sequences with no epitope structure must give nothing, each for its own reason

checks.name: positive and negative are separated
checks.why: this is the comparison C-ImmSim failed: an antigen and a housekeeping protein must not come out the same

checks.name: the epitopes come from the sequence, not the composition
checks.detail: SARS-CoV-2 spike: 0.0% of epitopes survive shuffling; response 5,732 vs 5,390; ovalbumin: 0.0% of epitopes survive shuffling; response 5,094 vs 5,019
checks.why: a shuffled protein has identical composition, so if the same peptides came back the model would be counting residues. It is EXPECTED that a shuffled protein is still immunogenic - it is still foreign - so the magnitudes are reported, not asserted on

checks.name: an anchor substitution destroys binding, a non-anchor one does not
checks.detail: predicted affinity worsens 26.7-fold when an anchor residue is changed, against 1.3-fold for a residue pointing at the T cell (n=52 and 52 substitutions)
checks.why: measured on the peptide itself, where it cannot be hidden by a whole-protein response that saturates. This is the check that the model has learned where the MHC groove grips

limitations.name: a single substitution does not move the whole-protein response
limitations.detail: SARS-CoV-2 spike: anchor 0.09%, non-anchor 0.1%, random 0.0%; ovalbumin: anchor -0.49%, non-anchor 0.57%, random 0.03%
limitations.why: an antigen with thousands of predicted binders does not notice losing one, so escape has to be studied at the epitope, not by re-simulating the mutated protein and comparing totals
